items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-06-06
items.q: Punch Miller to me is as near to playing the style that Buddy played than anybody else that I heard.

ctx.x: Do you remember anything about his style? Like you know, was he a high note man?

No, not a high note man. In those days trumpet players didn't play high notes. They had more of a running style. You mentioned the trumpet player the other day, Punch. Punch Miller. Do you remember Punch Miller? Sure. Well Punch Miller to me is as near to playing the style that Buddy played than anybody else that I heard. A style similar to what he's playing. Now Punch, don't misunderstand me, now Punch isn't copying Buddy PT. He's playing his style. But he gives you an idea what Buddy actually played. Oh he was…
Oh, there's something else that I told you I saw, I was talking to Emmanuel Sales the other day.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: I took Punch Miller to my house and, uh, entertained him.

ctx.x: Did you ever hear Oak's bass in Texas?

No, but I, I, I know that he did come to Texas. And Punch Miller came to Texas. And, uh, I, I took Punch Miller to my house and, uh, entertained him. And he was traveling with one of these two of these shows.
And he played in the Oakland County. And the city. You know, he kind of learned. That's right. He, he went, he lived in Houston for a while. I don't remember who he played with.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-27
items.q: Punch Miller, when Punch was young, he copied Buddy B.T. style as close as he could.

ctx.x: Like you go over there and you hear Buddy. Is there anybody on the record that sounds like Buddy that you've ever heard?

Not that I can recall right now. But I tell you what. Punch Miller, when Punch was young, he copied Buddy B.T. style as close as he could. But today, no I can't say that I, well, if you listen to my records, you'll hear a trumpet player named Billy Douglas. I think Billy Douglas is one of the greatest trumpet players I've ever heard in my life. Technical. The tonation wasn't the best in the world, but as a technical trumpet player, making things that we musicians hear are almost impossible, you get a vivid idea…
Do you think the musicians are a hack of the play of that kind of music?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: Punch Miller was a guy that amazed me with what he could do with those three vows.

ctx.x: I wonder if he knew much about chords or if it was all by ear or what?

Well, for what he was playing, he must have known something somehow. Art White was strictly a gift to him because he, well the same with Punch. Punch Miller was a guy that amazed me with what he could do with those three vows. Because his vows were, was one of these real fast-fingering things and there was a lot of, a lot of feeling to it. Not just a lot of notes, there was a lot of feeling coming out of the horn. And here's some of these trumpet players make all of these notes, a thousand notes. And there's no…
Have you ever heard of him? I know him, but I never heard of him play because he quit long before.
